tldr: Late October brought three Show HN projects pitching a control room or control plane for LLM agents: God, flightdeck, and Omneum. On Nov 4 the vLLM blog introduced Kinference, an open source inference control plane for vLLM on Kubernetes.
whats_new: OpenAI published two Control Room posts on Nov 9: a central system that tracks model workloads across its research infrastructure and can rapidly stop them when safety or security concerns arise.
why_it_matters: The label now spans three layers: agent observability, inference serving, and kill-switch control over training and research workloads. Check which layer a "control plane" actually governs before adopting it.

status.detail: Independent projects keep using "control plane" or "control room" for different layers; OpenAI's Control Room is the latest and an internal system, not a product.

beats.headline: Three Show HN projects pitch control surfaces for LLM agents
beats.summary: A real-time control room for agent societies, an observability and control plane for agents, and a local text-blind context control plane.

beats.headline: Kinference brings an open source control plane to vLLM on Kubernetes
beats.summary: Token rate limiting, tenant usage and cost tracking, and load balancing for scalable inference platforms.

beats.headline: OpenAI's Control Room tracks and can stop model workloads
beats.summary: Two posts on Nov 9 describe human control over AI workloads across OpenAI's research infrastructure.

open_questions: Does Kinference see adoption or contributions beyond its launch post on the vLLM blog?
Does OpenAI publish technical detail on how Control Room stops workloads, such as triggers or approval paths?
Do the Show HN projects (God, flightdeck, Omneum) gain users or contributors after their launch posts?
Do other labs describe comparable workload tracking and stop controls?
take_for_builders: If you run vLLM on Kubernetes, evaluate Kinference for per-tenant rate limits and cost tracking in a staging cluster. Treat the Show HN agent tools as early experiments and OpenAI's Control Room as a design reference, not something you can deploy.
